# UTI (Item Template) File Format

The UTI (Item Template) file format is a [GFF-based](gff.md) template format used in *Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic* (KotOR) and *The Sith Lords* (TSL) to define item properties, stats, and behaviors. UTI files serve as blueprints for items that can be instantiated in the game world, equipped by characters, or stored in inventories.

## File Structure

UTI files follow the standard [GFF format](gff.md) structure with a specific set of fields for item templates. The file contains both template fields (present in the original UTI file) and runtime fields (added when the item is instantiated in the game).

## Template Fields (Original UTI File)

These fields are present in the original UTI template file and define the item's base properties.

### Basic Information
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `TemplateResRef` | RESREF | Resource reference for the template |
| `LocalizedName` | CExoLocString | Localized display name |
| `Description` | CExoLocString | Item description |
| `DescIdentified` | CExoLocString | Description when identified |
| `BaseItem` | INT | Reference to [baseitems.2da](2da.md) entry |
| `ItemClass` | CExoString | Item class identifier |

### Visual Properties
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `ModelVariation` | BYTE | 3D model variation (1-255) |
| `TextureVar` | BYTE | Texture variation (1-255) |
| `PaletteID` | BYTE | Color palette identifier |
| `EquippedRes` | RESREF | 3D model when equipped |
| `InventoryRes` | RESREF | 2D icon when in inventory |

### Item Classification
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `ItemType` | BYTE | Type of item (weapon, armor, etc.) |
| `WeaponType` | BYTE | Weapon type classification |
| `WeaponWield` | BYTE | How the weapon is wielded |
| `RangedWeapon` | BYTE | Whether it's a ranged weapon |
| `WeaponSize` | BYTE | Size category of the weapon |

### Combat Properties
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `DamageFlags` | DWORD | Damage type flags |
| `NumDice` | BYTE | Number of damage dice |
| `DieToRoll` | BYTE | Type of dice to roll |
| `CriticalThreat` | BYTE | Critical threat range |
| `CriticalHitMultiplier` | BYTE | Critical hit damage multiplier |
| `MaxAttackRange` | FLOAT | Maximum attack range |
| `PrefAttackDist` | FLOAT | Preferred attack distance |
| `MinRange` | FLOAT | Minimum attack range |
| `MaxRange` | FLOAT | Maximum attack range |

### Usage Restrictions
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `RequiredFeat0` | INT | Required feat 1 |
| `RequiredFeat1` | INT | Required feat 2 |
| `RequiredFeat2` | INT | Required feat 3 |
| `RequiredFeat3` | INT | Required feat 4 |
| `RequiredFeat4` | INT | Required feat 5 |
| `RequiredClass` | BYTE | Required character class |
| `RequiredAlign` | BYTE | Required alignment |
| `RequiredAlignGroup` | BYTE | Required alignment group |

### Script References
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `OnEquip` | RESREF | Script to run when equipped |
| `OnUnEquip` | RESREF | Script to run when unequipped |
| `OnActivate` | RESREF | Script to run when activated |
| `OnUserDefined` | RESREF | User-defined script |

## Runtime Fields (Added During Gameplay)

When a UTI item is instantiated in the game world or saved in a save game, additional fields are added:

### Instance Identification
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `ObjectId` | DWORD | Unique object identifier in the game world |

### Item State
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `Identified` | BYTE | Whether the item has been identified |
| `Stolen` | BYTE | Whether the item was stolen |
| `Plot` | BYTE | Whether the item is plot-critical |
| `Dropable` | BYTE | Whether the item can be dropped |
| `Pickpocketable` | BYTE | Whether the item can be pickpocketed |

### Item Properties
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `StackSize` | WORD | Number of items in the stack |
| `Charges` | BYTE | Current number of charges |
| `MaxCharges` | BYTE | Maximum number of charges |
| `Cost` | DWORD | Base cost of the item |
| `AddCost` | DWORD | Additional cost modifiers |

### Visual State
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `ModelVariation` | BYTE | Current model variation |
| `TextureVariation` | BYTE | Current texture variation |

### Upgrade System
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `Upgrades` | DWORD | Number of upgrades applied |
| `UpgradeLevel` | BYTE | Current upgrade level |
| `UpgradeSlot0` | INT | Upgrade in slot 0 |
| `UpgradeSlot1` | INT | Upgrade in slot 1 |
| `UpgradeSlot2` | INT | Upgrade in slot 2 |
| `UpgradeSlot3` | INT | Upgrade in slot 3 |
| `UpgradeSlot4` | INT | Upgrade in slot 4 |
| `UpgradeSlot5` | INT | Upgrade in slot 5 |

### Localized Text
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `Description` | CExoLocString | Current description |
| `DescIdentified` | CExoLocString | Identified description |
| `LocalizedName` | CExoLocString | Current display name |

### Properties List
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `PropertiesList` | LIST | List of item properties (enchantments, etc.) |

### Position and Orientation
| Field Name | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| `XPosition` | FLOAT | X coordinate in world |
| `YPosition` | FLOAT | Y coordinate in world |
| `ZPosition` | FLOAT | Z coordinate in world |
| `XOrientation` | FLOAT | X rotation in radians |
| `YOrientation` | FLOAT | Y rotation in radians |
| `ZOrientation` | FLOAT | Z rotation in radians |

## Item Properties System

Items can have various properties that modify their behavior:

### Property Types
- **Enchantment Bonuses**: Stat bonuses, damage bonuses, etc.
- **Special Abilities**: Cast spell, disguise, etc.
- **Restrictions**: Class restrictions, alignment restrictions
- **Visual Effects**: Glow effects, particle effects

### Property Structure
Each property in the `PropertiesList` contains:
- **Property Name**: Type of property
- **Sub Type**: Specific variant of the property
- **Value**: Numerical value for the property
- **Duration**: How long the property lasts

## File Loading Process

1. **Template Loading**: Load the UTI template file
2. **Base Item Resolution**: Resolve the `BaseItem` reference to [baseitems.2da](2da.md)
3. **Property Initialization**: Initialize item properties from template
4. **Runtime Field Addition**: Add runtime fields when instantiated
5. **Model Loading**: Load 3D models and textures
6. **Script Compilation**: Compile associated scripts

## Usage in Game

UTI files are used for:

- **Weapons**: Swords, blasters, lightsabers, etc.
- **Armor**: Clothing, armor pieces, robes
- **Accessories**: Belts, gloves, boots, etc.
- **Consumables**: Medpacs, stimulants, grenades
- **Miscellaneous**: Keys, quest items, components
- **Upgrade Components**: Weapon and armor upgrades

## Item Categories

### Weapons
- **Melee Weapons**: Swords, staffs, vibroblades
- **Ranged Weapons**: Blasters, rifles, pistols
- **Lightsabers**: Single, double, short lightsabers
- **Thrown Weapons**: Grenades, thermal detonators

### Armor
- **Light Armor**: Clothing, light protective gear
- **Medium Armor**: Combat suits, medium protection
- **Heavy Armor**: Heavy combat armor, power armor
- **Robes**: Jedi robes, Sith robes, special clothing

### Accessories
- **Belts**: Utility belts, weapon belts
- **Gloves**: Combat gloves, utility gloves
- **Boots**: Combat boots, utility boots
- **Implants**: Cybernetic enhancements

## Technical Notes

- **GFF Format**: UTI files use the standard GFF binary format
- **Endianness**: All multi-byte values are stored in little-endian format
- **String Encoding**: Text fields use UTF-8 encoding
- **Resource References**: RESREF fields are 16-byte null-padded strings
- **Localization**: CExoLocString fields support multiple languages
- **Template Inheritance**: Items inherit properties from their base item type

## Related File Formats

- **[GFF](gff.md)** - Base format for UTI files
- **[2DA](2da.md)** - [baseitems.2da](2da.md) defines base item properties
- **[TLK](tlk.md)** - Localized strings for item names and descriptions
- **[MDL](mdl.md)** - 3D models for equipped items
- **[TPC](tpc.md)** - Textures for item models and icons
- **[ERF](erf.md)** - Archive format that contains UTI files
- **[KEY](key.md)** - Resource index that references UTI files

# WOK (Walkmesh)

The WOK (Walkmesh) file format is used in *Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic* (KotOR) to define navigable areas within game environments. Walkmesh files determine where characters can walk, run, and interact within 3D scenes, ensuring realistic character movement and preventing characters from walking through walls or floating in mid-air.

## Overview

Walkmesh files are essential for proper game functionality as they define the collision boundaries and walkable surfaces in 3D environments. They work in conjunction with area models to create a complete navigable space for characters and NPCs.

## File Structure

The WOK file format is a binary format that stores 3D geometry data optimized for pathfinding and collision detection.

## Binary File Structure

### Header (136 bytes)
| Offset | Size | Type | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| 0x00   | 4    | Char[4] | File signature ("WOK ") |
| 0x04   | 4    | Char[4] | Version (typically "V1.0") |
| 0x08   | 4    | UInt32 | Walkmesh type (0x00 = NONE, 0x01 = AABB) |
| 0x0C   | 48   | Byte[48] | Reserved padding |
| 0x3C   | 4    | Float32 | Position X |
| 0x40   | 4    | Float32 | Position Y |
| 0x44   | 4    | Float32 | Position Z |
| 0x48   | 4    | UInt32 | Vertex count |
| 0x4C   | 4    | UInt32 | Vertex data offset |
| 0x50   | 4    | UInt32 | Face count |
| 0x54   | 4    | UInt32 | Face data offset |
| 0x58   | 4    | UInt32 | Walk types offset |
| 0x5C   | 4    | UInt32 | Normals offset |
| 0x60   | 4    | UInt32 | Face plane coefficients offset |
| 0x64   | 4    | UInt32 | AABB count |
| 0x68   | 4    | UInt32 | AABB data offset |
| 0x6C   | 4    | UInt32 | Unknown entry |
| 0x70   | 4    | UInt32 | Walkable faces adjacency matrix count |
| 0x74   | 4    | UInt32 | Walkable faces adjacency matrix offset |
| 0x78   | 4    | UInt32 | Edge count |
| 0x7C   | 4    | UInt32 | Edge data offset |
| 0x80   | 4    | UInt32 | Perimeter count |
| 0x84   | 4    | UInt32 | Perimeter data offset |

### Vertex Data Block
Array of 3D coordinates defining the points of the walkmesh. Each vertex is 12 bytes:

| Offset | Size | Type | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| 0x00   | 4    | Float32 | X coordinate |
| 0x04   | 4    | Float32 | Y coordinate |
| 0x08   | 4    | Float32 | Z coordinate |

**Total size per vertex**: 12 bytes

### Face Data Block
Array of triangular faces that define walkable surfaces. Each face is 12 bytes:

| Offset | Size | Type | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| 0x00   | 4    | UInt32 | Vertex 1 index |
| 0x04   | 4    | UInt32 | Vertex 2 index |
| 0x08   | 4    | UInt32 | Vertex 3 index |

**Total size per face**: 12 bytes

### Walk Types Block
Array of surface material indices for each face. Each entry is 4 bytes:

| Offset | Size | Type | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| 0x00   | 4    | UInt32 | Surface material index |

**Total size per walk type**: 4 bytes

### Normals Block
Array of face normals. Each normal is 12 bytes:

| Offset | Size | Type | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| 0x00   | 4    | Float32 | Normal X |
| 0x04   | 4    | Float32 | Normal Y |
| 0x08   | 4    | Float32 | Normal Z |

**Total size per normal**: 12 bytes

### Face Plane Coefficients Block
Array of plane coefficients for each face. Each entry is 4 bytes:

| Offset | Size | Type | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| 0x00   | 4    | Float32 | Plane coefficient |

**Total size per coefficient**: 4 bytes

### AABB (Axis-Aligned Bounding Box) Block
Array of AABB nodes for collision detection. Each AABB is 44 bytes:

| Offset | Size | Type | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| 0x00   | 4    | Float32 | Min X |
| 0x04   | 4    | Float32 | Min Y |
| 0x08   | 4    | Float32 | Min Z |
| 0x0C   | 4    | Float32 | Max X |
| 0x10   | 4    | Float32 | Max Y |
| 0x14   | 4    | Float32 | Max Z |
| 0x18   | 4    | UInt32 | Face index |
| 0x1C   | 4    | UInt32 | Unknown fixed value |
| 0x20   | 4    | UInt32 | Most significant plane |
| 0x24   | 4    | UInt32 | Left node offset |
| 0x28   | 4    | UInt32 | Right node offset |

**Total size per AABB**: 44 bytes

### Walkable Faces Adjacency Matrix Block
Array of adjacency information for walkable faces. Each entry is 12 bytes:

| Offset | Size | Type | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| 0x00   | 4    | UInt32 | Adjacent face 1 index |
| 0x04   | 4    | UInt32 | Adjacent face 2 index |
| 0x08   | 4    | UInt32 | Adjacent face 3 index |

**Total size per adjacency entry**: 12 bytes

### Edge Data Block
Array of edges connecting faces for room transitions. Each edge is 8 bytes:

| Offset | Size | Type | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| 0x00   | 4    | UInt32 | Edge index |
| 0x04   | 4    | UInt32 | Transition value |

**Total size per edge**: 8 bytes

### Perimeter Data Block
Array of perimeter definitions. Each perimeter entry is 4 bytes:

| Offset | Size | Type | Description |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| 0x00   | 4    | UInt32 | Edge offset |

**Total size per perimeter entry**: 4 bytes

## File Layout Summary

```
Offset 0x0000: Header (136 bytes)
Offset 0x0088: Vertex Data Block (vertex_count × 12 bytes)
Offset 0x????: Face Data Block (face_count × 12 bytes)
Offset 0x????: Walk Types Block (face_count × 4 bytes)
Offset 0x????: Normals Block (face_count × 12 bytes)
Offset 0x????: Face Plane Coefficients Block (face_count × 4 bytes)
Offset 0x????: AABB Block (aabb_count × 44 bytes)
Offset 0x????: Walkable Faces Adjacency Matrix Block (walkable_faces_count × 12 bytes)
Offset 0x????: Edge Data Block (edge_count × 8 bytes)
Offset 0x????: Perimeter Data Block (perimeter_count × 4 bytes)
```

## Walkmesh Types

The walkmesh type determines the collision detection method used:

| Type ID | Name | Description |
|---------|------|-------------|
| 0x00    | NONE | No special collision detection |
| 0x01    | AABB | Axis-Aligned Bounding Box collision detection |

## Data Type Definitions

### UInt32
- **Size**: 4 bytes
- **Range**: 0 to 4,294,967,295
- **Endianness**: Little-endian
- **Usage**: Counts, indices, IDs, flags

### Float32
- **Size**: 4 bytes
- **Range**: ±3.4 × 10^38
- **Precision**: ~7 decimal digits
- **Endianness**: Little-endian
- **Usage**: 3D coordinates

### Char[4]
- **Size**: 4 bytes
- **Encoding**: ASCII
- **Usage**: File signatures and version strings

### Byte[48]
- **Size**: 48 bytes
- **Usage**: Reserved padding space

## Surface Types

Walkmesh faces can have different surface types that affect gameplay:

| Type ID | Surface Type | Description |
|---------|--------------|-------------|
| 0x00    | Default      | Standard walkable surface |
| 0x01    | Metal        | Metallic surface (metal footstep sounds) |
| 0x02    | Stone        | Stone surface (stone footstep sounds) |
| 0x03    | Wood         | Wooden surface (wood footstep sounds) |
| 0x04    | Water        | Water surface (splash sounds) |
| 0x05    | Sand         | Sandy surface (sand footstep sounds) |
| 0x06    | Grass        | Grass surface (grass footstep sounds) |
| 0x07    | Dirt         | Dirt surface (dirt footstep sounds) |
| 0x08    | Ice          | Icy surface (ice footstep sounds) |
| 0x09    | Snow         | Snowy surface (snow footstep sounds) |
| 0x0A    | Mud          | Muddy surface (mud footstep sounds) |
| 0x0B    | Leaves       | Leaves surface (leaves footstep sounds) |
| 0x0C    | Lava         | Lava surface (lava footstep sounds) |
| 0x0D    | BottomlessPit | Bottomless pit surface (bottomless pit footstep sounds) |
| 0x0E    | DeepWater    | Deep water surface (deep water footstep sounds) |
| 0x0F    | Door         | Door surface (door footstep sounds) |
| 0x10    | NonWalkGrass | Non-walkable grass surface (non-walkable grass footstep sounds) |
| 0x1E    | Trigger      | Trigger surface (trigger footstep sounds) |

## Face Flags

Faces can have various flags that affect their behavior:

| Flag | Name | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| 0x01 | Walkable | Face is walkable by characters |
| 0x02 | Door | Face represents a door or portal |
| 0x04 | Trigger | Face can trigger events |
| 0x08 | Obstacle | Face blocks character movement |
| 0x10 | Water | Face is water surface |
| 0x20 | Lava | Face is lava surface (damaging) |
| 0x40 | Pits | Face is a pit (falling damage) |
| 0x80 | Stairs | Face represents stairs |

## Room System

The walkmesh is divided into rooms for efficient pathfinding and area management:

- **Room Boundaries**: Each room has defined boundaries within the walkmesh
- **Room Transitions**: Edges define transitions between rooms
- **Pathfinding**: Characters can only pathfind within the same room
- **Area Loading**: Rooms can be loaded/unloaded independently

## Usage in KotOR

### Area Files
- WOK files are associated with area models (ARE files)
- Each area typically has one corresponding WOK file
- File naming convention: `area_name.wok`

### Character Movement
- Characters can only move on walkable faces
- Surface types determine footstep sounds
- Face flags control special behaviors (doors, triggers, etc.)

### Pathfinding
- AI uses walkmesh for navigation
- Characters avoid non-walkable faces
- Room system optimizes pathfinding calculations

## Tools and Utilities

### WalkSwitch - Collision Map Editor
- **Purpose**: View and edit WOK files
- **Features**: 
  - Visual walkmesh display
  - Surface type editing
  - Room adjacency editing
  - Face flag modification

### MDLEdit
- **Purpose**: Model editor with walkmesh support
- **Features**:
  - Load and edit 3D models
  - Associated walkmesh data
  - Model-walkmesh alignment

### GFF Editor
- **Purpose**: General file format editor
- **Features**:
  - Binary file analysis
  - Data structure inspection
  - Hex editing capabilities

## Modding Considerations

### Creating New Areas
1. Design the 3D area model
2. Create corresponding walkmesh
3. Ensure walkmesh aligns with model geometry
4. Set appropriate surface types and flags
5. Define room boundaries and transitions

### Editing Existing Areas
1. Load the WOK file in WalkSwitch
2. Modify walkable areas as needed
3. Update surface types for new materials
4. Adjust room boundaries if necessary
5. Test character movement in-game

### Common Issues
- **Misaligned walkmesh**: Characters walk through walls or float
- **Missing faces**: Characters fall through the floor
- **Wrong surface types**: Incorrect footstep sounds
- **Room boundary problems**: Pathfinding issues between areas

## Technical Notes

- All coordinates are in 3D world space
- Face normals determine which side is walkable
- Room adjacency is crucial for proper pathfinding
- Surface types affect audio and visual effects
- Face flags control special gameplay mechanics

## Practical Examples

### Reading a WOK File (Pseudocode)

```c
// Read header
char signature[4];
char version[4];
uint32_t walkmesh_type;
uint8_t reserved[48];
float position[3];
uint32_t vertex_count;
uint32_t vertex_offset;
// ... other header fields

// Read vertices
seek(vertex_offset);
for (int i = 0; i < vertex_count; i++) {
    float x = read_float32();
    float y = read_float32();
    float z = read_float32();
    vertices[i] = {x, y, z};
}

// Read faces
seek(face_offset);
for (int i = 0; i < face_count; i++) {
    uint32_t a = read_uint32();
    uint32_t b = read_uint32();
    uint32_t c = read_uint32();
    faces[i] = {a, b, c};
}

// Read walk types
seek(walk_types_offset);
for (int i = 0; i < face_count; i++) {
    uint32_t material_index = read_uint32();
    walk_types[i] = material_index;
}
```

### Calculating Face Normals

```c
Vector3 calculate_face_normal(Vector3 v1, Vector3 v2, Vector3 v3) {
    Vector3 edge1 = v2 - v1;
    Vector3 edge2 = v3 - v1;
    Vector3 normal = cross_product(edge1, edge2);
    return normalize(normal);
}
```

### Checking Point Walkability

```c
bool is_point_walkable(Vector3 point, Walkmesh* walkmesh) {
    for (int i = 0; i < walkmesh->face_count; i++) {
        Face face = walkmesh->faces[i];
        Vector3 v1 = walkmesh->vertices[face.a];
        Vector3 v2 = walkmesh->vertices[face.b];
        Vector3 v3 = walkmesh->vertices[face.c];
        
        if (point_in_triangle_2d(point, v1, v2, v3)) {
            uint32_t material_index = walkmesh->walk_types[i];
            SurfaceMaterial* material = get_surface_material(material_index);
            return material->walkable;
        }
    }
    return false;
}
```

- **WalkSwitch Tool**: Collision Map Editor for WOK files
- **MDLEdit**: Model editor with walkmesh support
- **GFF Editor**: General file format editor
